name: Hochhaus Neue Donau
key_features: Harry Seidler's 34-storey residential tower in Vienna's Donau City, 150 metres tall and currently Austria's third tallest building.

name: Ito-toren
key_features: Toyo Ito's 100-metre office tower in Amsterdam's Zuidas, part of the Mahler4 complex.

name: Torre Picasso
key_features: Minoru Yamasaki's 43-floor tower beside Pablo Picasso Square in Madrid's AZCA, the city's tallest from 1988 to 2007.

name: Mode Gakuen Spiral Towers
key_features: Nagoya's 170-metre, 36-storey school tower, home to three vocational schools and one of the city's tallest buildings.

name: Hagia Sophia Hurrem Sultan Bathhouse
key_features: Sinan's 16th-century bath for Hürrem Sultan, built on the site of the ancient Baths of Zeuxippus.

name: Sinan Pasha Mosque (Istanbul)
key_features: Sinan's mosque in Beşiktaş, built for Admiral Sinan Pasha, with Barbaros Hayrettin Pasha's tomb across the street.

name: Hôtel Solvay
key_features: Victor Horta's Art Nouveau town house in Brussels, designed for Armand Solvay and built 1895–1900.

name: University of Science and Technology, Houari Boumediene
key_features: Niemeyer's university campus near Algiers, inaugurated in 1974.

name: Ennis House
key_features: Wright's Mayan Revival house of concrete textile blocks in Los Angeles, completed in 1925.

name: Frank Lloyd Wright Home and Studio
key_features: Wright's home and studio in Oak Park, built in 1889 and expanded with a Prairie-style studio.

name: Süleymaniye Hamam
key_features: Sinan's 1557 bathhouse in Istanbul's Süleymaniye complex, arched and domed, with marble inlay on its walls.

name: Otaniemi water tower
key_features: Aalto's 1971 water tower in Otaniemi, a 45-metre landmark stacking a water tank on a free-form building.

name: Waldspirale
key_features: Hundertwasser's 2000 Darmstadt housing complex, with a spiral plan and a green roof.

name: Osaka Maritime Museum
key_features: Domed museum on reclaimed land in Osaka Bay, built to resist quakes, waves and wind; closed since 2013.

name: The Cenotaph
key_features: Lutyens's national war memorial on Whitehall, unveiled in 1920; its empty-tomb form symbolises the absent dead.

name: Tel Aviv Performing Arts Center
key_features: Tel Aviv's performing arts centre on King Saul Boulevard, home of the Israeli Opera; opened 1994.

name: Palazzo dello Strozzino
key_features: A Renaissance stone palace on Piazza degli Strozzi, diagonal to the larger Palazzo Strozzi.

name: Kudrinskaya Square Building
key_features: One of the Seven Sisters, Moscow's Stalinist skyscrapers, designed by Posokhin and Mndoyants.

name: Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
key_features: Lisbon's museum of art, architecture and technology, a 2016 work by Amanda Levete (AL_A).

name: Forum Groningen
key_features: A cultural centre in Groningen with a library, cinema, museums and a rooftop bar, opened in 2019.

name: Saskatchewan Legislative Building
key_features: Saskatchewan's 1912 Legislative Building in Regina, by the Maxwell brothers, houses the Legislative Assembly.

name: Nuevos Ministerios
key_features: Madrid's government complex, begun in 1933 by Secundino Zuazo and completed in 1942.

name: Hansahochhaus
key_features: Cologne's first skyscraper and one of Germany's first, an Expressionist office building built 1924–25.

name: Oakland City Hall
key_features: The first high-rise government building in the United States, and once the tallest west of the Mississippi.

name: Rosenbad
key_features: Stockholm's government seat, an Art Nouveau building by Ferdinand Boberg, completed in 1902.

name: Perelman Performing Arts Center
key_features: Joshua Ramus's performing arts center on the World Trade Center site, chosen in 2015 after earlier plans were scrapped.

name: Tournay Abbey
key_features: An active Benedictine monastery of about 20 monks; the new building was completed in 1958.

name: Heureka
key_features: A science centre by Heikkinen–Komonen Architects, opened in 1989 beside the Keravanjoki river and the Main Line railway.

name: Historical Museum of the Palatinate
key_features: A history museum across the square from Speyer Cathedral, with about a million artifacts.

name: Old Faithful Inn
key_features: A log hotel in Yellowstone, the first of the great park lodges and a National Park Service Rustic landmark.

name: Museum Yamato Bunkakan
key_features: Museum of Asian art in Nara, established in 1960 for the private collection of the Kintetsu railway company.

name: Vatroslav Lisinski Concert Hall
key_features: Concert hall and convention centre with 1,841 and 305 seat halls and a lobby that doubles as an exhibition area.

name: Jewish Museum Munich
key_features: Part of the Jewish Center on Sankt-Jakobs-Platz, between the Ohel Jakob synagogue and the community centre; built 2004 to 2007.

name: Royal Armouries Museum
key_features: A £42.5 million purpose-built museum at Leeds Dock, opened in 1996 for the national collection of arms and armour.

name: Monona Terrace
key_features: Frank Lloyd Wright's 1938 design for a lakeshore convention centre, opened in 1997 on Lake Monona.

name: Minnaert building
by: Neutelings Riedijk Architects, Willem Jan Neutelings, Michiel Riedijk
key_features: Campus building named after astronomer Marcel Minnaert, opened in 1997 for Utrecht University's science faculties.

name: Zénith de Lille
key_features: Rem Koolhaas's arena in Lille, seating up to 7,000 and opened in 1994 within the Lille Grand Palais complex.

name: He Art Museum
key_features: Tadao Ando's privately funded non-profit museum in Foshan, designed by a Pritzker Prize winner.

name: Paraninfo de la Universidad del País Vasco
key_features: Álvaro Siza's 2010 hall for the Basque Country university, faced in grey handmade tiles and white marble.

name: Kita des Deutschen Bundestages
key_features: Peichl's Berlin nursery for Bundestag families, shaped like a ship moored on the Spree, with lively colour.

name: Fukuoka Camera Museum
key_features: Tadao Ando's camera and photography museum in Takaoka, Toyama.

name: Hagi Uragami Museum
key_features: A prefectural art museum in Hagi, one of several cultural facilities planned to be spread evenly across Yamaguchi Prefecture.

name: ONIKURU
key_features: A civic complex in Ibaraki with a hall, library, children's centre, indoor playground and planetarium.

name: Skylight
key_features: A 'city within a city' in Frankfurt: offices, shops and flats around a 66-metre residential tower.

name: New Synagogue (Mainz)
key_features: A Modernist-styled synagogue and community centre on the site of Mainz's synagogue destroyed in 1938.

name: Paulinum (University of Leipzig)
key_features: Erick van Egeraat's university hall on the old Paulinerkirche site; the church was destroyed in 1968.

name: Spiral House
key_features: An apartment complex spiralling upward, its terraced roofs used as living space, as in Arab villages.

name: STC Group
by: Neutelings Riedijk Architects, Willem Jan Neutelings, Michiel Riedijk
key_features: Rotterdam headquarters of the Shipping and Transport College Group, a maritime transport and logistics education provider.

name: Konzerthaus Blaibach
key_features: Concert house in the village of Blaibach in the Upper Palatinate, for concerts, cultural events and exhibitions.

name: Rio Art Museum
key_features: Rio's art museum, opened in 2013, planned by Jacobsen Arquitetura around a flow system for the whole site.

name: Seinäjoki City Theatre
key_features: Alvar and Elissa Aalto's municipal theatre for the Finnish city of Seinäjoki.

name: Norman Lykes House
key_features: Wright's last house design, a circular two-story home on a mountain slope, finished in 1967 by his onetime apprentice.

name: Villa of Viktor Bauer
key_features: Loos's puristic villa for a sugar-refinery director in Hrušovany, the only large Loos work in Moravia.

name: Haus Scheu
key_features: Loos's Vienna house, one of the first modern buildings to use a flat roof.

name: Jonson Gallery
key_features: John Gaw Meem's Pueblo Revival home and gallery for the modernist painter Raymond Jonson, on a hillside.

name: Villa Urbig
key_features: Mies van der Rohe's villa on the Griebnitzsee, in Potsdam's former Neubabelsberg villa colony.

name: Vakantiehuisjes (Rietveld)
key_features: One of six Rietveld cottages of 1951 for factory staff; one was moved to the Arnhem open-air museum.

name: Palazzo degli Affari
key_features: Carlo Mollino's Turin chamber of commerce offices, a bold structural solution set against its surroundings.

name: Stillman House I
key_features: Breuer's 1950 house in Litchfield, one of three Breuer commissions on the site; its pool wall has a Calder mural.

name: Harold C. Bradley House
key_features: One of few residential designs by Louis Sullivan, a Prairie School house and a National Historic Landmark.

name: Offenbarungskirche
key_features: One of the postwar emergency churches (Notkirchen) by Bauhaus-trained Otto Bartning, part of a community centre.

name: Ruderzentrum Blasewitz
key_features: A rowing centre roofed by four hyperbolic paraboloid shells, tilted inwards to let in more daylight.

name: Villa Haas
key_features: A functionalist villa in Brno's Pisárky district, built 1928–1930 for the head of a bank branch.

name: Église Sainte-Thérèse-de-l'Enfant-Jésus de Metz
key_features: Roger-Henri Expert's church in Metz, with stained glass by Nicolas Untersteller in a personal, new technique.

name: Naturtheater Grötzingen
key_features: A 1954 thin concrete shell over an open-air sylvan theatre that seats 850.

name: La Spezia Cathedral
key_features: A Roman Catholic cathedral built 1956–1975 to designs by Adalberto Libera.

name: Vila Franze Strosse
key_features: A 1923–25 villa in Liberec by Thilo Schoder, its rounded forms evoking a ship.

name: International Conference Center Hiroshima
key_features: A convention centre with a multipurpose hall in central Hiroshima, designed by Kenzō Tange.

name: ONYX theater
key_features: A performance venue in Saint-Herblain, created in 1988 and now run by the city.

name: Vila Tychonova 4
key_features: The southern half of a double villa in Prague's Hradčany by Josef Gočár, protected since 1958.

name: Villa Kenwin
key_features: A Bauhaus-style villa in La Tour-de-Peilz by Hermann Henselmann and Alexander Ferenczy.

name: WRVA Building
key_features: Built for a radio station and designed by Philip Johnson, called one of Richmond's most important mid-century landmarks.

name: Joseph H. Brown Elementary School
key_features: A 1937 Philadelphia school by the district's main architect, an exemplar of Art Deco and Moderne design.

name: Hochhaus Württembergische Straße 6
key_features: West Berlin's first office high-rise, a pioneering example of postwar modernism with open, transparent architecture.

name: Schönberg Tower
key_features: A 26.4 m lookout tower from 1905 by the well-known architect Theodor Fischer, a landmark of Pfullingen.

name: Theodore Baird Residence
by: Frank Lloyd Wright, William Wesley Peters
key_features: The only Frank Lloyd Wright design in Massachusetts, a Usonian house partly built at a New Jersey factory.

name: Jyväskylä Defence Corps Building
key_features: Aalto's Defence Corps building in central Jyväskylä, also called the Government Building, completed in 1929.

name: Kunstgebäude Stuttgart
key_features: Theodor Fischer's Kunstgebäude on Stuttgart's Schlossplatz, opened in 1913, with sculpted façade and colonnade.

name: Suchardova vila
key_features: Jan Kotěra's villa and studio for the sculptor Stanislav Sucharda and his family, built 1904–1907 in Prague.

name: Palace Theatre (Marion, Ohio)
key_features: A 1928 atmospheric movie palace, one of the last of its style in the US, on the National Register.

name: St. Mauritius
key_features: A Brutalist church centre in Munich's Moosach district, completed in 1967.

name: Yorkville Library
key_features: Manhattan's first Carnegie library, designed by James Brown Lord in Italian Renaissance style with a limestone facade.

name: Shikoku Mura Gallery
key_features: Ando's gallery on a hillside in Shikoku Mura, with a water garden and a view over Takamatsu.

name: Postgebouw van Oostende
key_features: Ostend's former post office, built 1947–1953 by Gaston Eysselinck and now a cultural centre.

name: Our Lady of Good Counsel Church, Glasgow
key_features: A Glasgow Roman Catholic parish church in Dennistoun, listed Category A.

name: Königliche Anatomie
key_features: Among the first large reinforced-concrete buildings in Germany, built 1905–1907 by Max Littmann.

name: Villa Carl (Feldafing)
key_features: Riemerschmid's 1910–12 Jugendstil villa in Feldafing, with its fully preserved original interior.

name: Guildford Cathedral
key_features: The last Church of England cathedral consecrated on a new site, built 1936–1961 to Edward Maufe's design.

name: Villa Kroha
key_features: Architect Jiří Kroha's own functionalist family house in Brno, built 1928–1930.

name: Villa Patočka
key_features: Jiří Kroha's 1935–36 functionalist villa in Brno's Pod vodojemem colony.

name: Freibad Letzigraben
key_features: Max Frisch's only major building, a 1949 Landi-style open-air bath in Zürich with a garden by Gustav Ammann.

name: Skogskapellet
key_features: Gunnar Asplund's first chapel at Skogskyrkogården, now part of a Swedish World Heritage site.

name: Nymble
key_features: The KTH student union house in Stockholm, built 1928–1930 by Markelius and Åhrén and marked as culturally valuable in 2012.

name: Finnish Pavilion, Venice Biennale
key_features: Alvar Aalto's pavilion housing Finland's national representation at the Venice Biennale, beside the shared Nordic pavilion.

name: Renaat Braem House
key_features: Renaat Braem's own studio house in Antwerp, designed by himself and later turned into a museum.

name: Einsteinhaus Caputh
key_features: A 1929 timber summer house at Caputh near Potsdam, home of Albert Einstein until 1932.

name: Koumi-machi Kōgen Museum of Art
key_features: A town-run art museum in Koumi.

name: Vilamajó House Museum
key_features: Julio Vilamajó's 1930 family house, the first modern dwelling opened as a museum in Uruguay.
